input: Draft a short pitch deck for investors

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number and type of slides included will fundamentally shape the structure and depth of the deck — a 5-slide teaser is very different from a 12-slide full pitch.
The target investor profile (angel, VC, strategic partner, crowd) determines the language, level of detail, and what to emphasise (e.g. traction vs. vision vs. financials).
Whether this is for a cold email attachment, a live presentation, or a demo day changes format, slide density, and how much text vs. visuals to use.
The funding stage and amount sought sets expectations around valuation, milestones, and the maturity of data the deck must present.
The business sector and the specific story angle (problem-first, traction-first, founder-first) dictates tone, terminology, and what to lead with.
Knowing the single most important outcome (e.g. secure a first meeting, close a round, get a warm intro) focuses what the deck must convince investors of.
The desired deliverable format (slide-by-slide outline, full written content, designed file, speaker notes) determines how much work is needed and what tool to use.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a Short Investor Pitch Deck
gold.taskDescription: Create a concise pitch deck designed to attract investment for the user's venture or project.

questions.title: How many slides should the deck contain?
questions.description: Clarify the intended length — e.g. a 5-slide teaser, a 10-slide standard pitch, or a 15-slide deep-dive — to set the structural scope.

questions.title: What type of investor is this deck targeting?
questions.description: Identify the audience — angel investors, early-stage VCs, growth-stage funds, strategic corporate partners — to calibrate language and emphasis.

questions.title: Where and how will this deck be presented or shared?
questions.description: Determine the delivery context — emailed cold as a PDF, shown live in a room, submitted to a demo day — to shape density and visual style.

questions.title: What funding stage and raise amount is this for?
questions.description: Establish the round size and stage (pre-seed, seed, Series A, etc.) so the deck can set appropriate financial expectations and milestones.

questions.title: What industry is the business in, and what is its core story?
questions.description: Understand the sector and the narrative angle — problem-driven, traction-driven, or founder-driven — to set the right tone and lead slide.

questions.title: What specific action should investors take after seeing this deck?
questions.description: Define the desired outcome — book a meeting, sign an NDA, commit capital — so the deck's call to action and persuasion arc are correctly targeted.

questions.title: What format should the final deliverable be in?
questions.description: Clarify whether the output should be a written slide-by-slide outline, full slide copy, speaker notes, or a ready-to-design structured document.
